process_observations.observation: The block was closed without touching the artefact: all four XML files are SHA-256 byte-identical to the blocked run, so the file that was rejected is the file that now passes.

The skill fix split a conflated code rather than relaxing a check - the stale-timeLength case that used to share W4 is now W7, still a strict-promoted WARN - so nothing that was a real failure stopped being one.
The calendar cross-reference --strict exists for is green: at build scope all four step-scope W6 findings clear and no W3 replaces them, and the whole documented ERROR set E1-E4 is clean.

The surviving INFO W4 asks the author to confirm the action-less design is intended; milestone-completion-decision.md already answers it, because D10 puts the CompletionDate writer in M4-S05's Apex and no clarification asks for a milestone notification.

Unchanged from the first run and not addressed by the skill fix: an EMEA-region case counts its first-response milestone on US Support hours while its escalation timer counts on EMEA Support hours via businessHoursSource=Case, so the two SLA clocks on one case pause on different holidays.
No step in this plan owns settings/Entitlement.settings-meta.xml, so enableEntitlements - without which every file in this step is inert - and enableMilestoneStoppedTime remain unscoped.

These processes are now built and will deploy active, but M4-S03 (the EntitlementId stamp) and M4-S05 (the CompletionDate writer) are both still pending, so until they land no case enters a process and any that did would never close its milestone.
The build's manifests remain split across two API versions - nine at 62.0 and four including this one at 67.0 - with no api_version key in plan.json to settle it.
Standard's minutesToComplete 720 is still DERIVED and not answered: nothing in this build converts '1 business day' into minutes, and 480 or a next-business-day promise are both defensible readings.
The declared mixed-case process file names still cannot be what a retrieve returns, because the guide derives the name as the lowercase NameNorm of <name>.
The one-calendar-per-process tension against Q51's Case-calendar authority is untouched by the skill fix and still needs adjudicating.
